A Texas school district is going all-in on iPad and MacBook Neo, spending $11 million. The Beaumont Independent School District has decided to ditch Chromebooks in favor of an Apple-exclusive setup, citing better reliability, lower costs, and superior performance.

According to the Beaumont Enterprise this week, the Beaumont Independent School District's board of trustees has approved a four-year, $11.19 million lease deal to upgrade its technology.

The deal includes 14,585 Apple devices for students and staff from pre-K through 12th grade. The new Apple gear will replace a fleet of aging Chromebooks, many of which are five years old. The district was spending nearly $500,000 a year just to repair and support those Chromebooks.

The new plan includes over 4,000 iPads for pre-K through 2nd grade students, and 9,500 MacBook Neo units for students in grades 3 through 12. The district has also set aside 1,000 MacBook Neo units for teachers.

After comparing the MacBook Neo against offerings from Lenovo and Asus, the district concluded that the MacBook Neo "was the top-performing and most reliable device among those evaluated." Apple's financing terms were also more favorable, and access to AppleCare was a factor as well.
